props.label: About Us
props.heading: A workshop, not a reselling showroom
props.body:
Sagar Furniture & Enterprises is a furniture manufacturing unit and showroom on Godhani Road, Nagpur, run by Sagar Ravindra Lande. We make furniture rather than resell it — boards are cut, edge-banded, assembled and finished in our own workshop, which is what lets us build to a size that does not exist in any catalogue.

That covers the whole home and office: modular kitchens and wardrobes, sofas and L-corner sets, beds including hydraulic storage beds, dining sets, TV units, CNC and Sagwan mandirs, office workstations and tables, and storage built into whatever space you have. We survey the site, draw the piece, put the actual material samples in front of you, and only start manufacturing once you have approved it.

Because the workshop is ours, a change of size, shutter or internal layout is a conversation rather than a refusal, and the quality of the work is ours to answer for. Delivery and installation across Nagpur are handled by our own team.

props.label: Our Services
props.heading: What we make and do
props.sub: Fifteen services covering the whole home and office — from a single mandir to a complete interior fit-out.

items.title: Customised Furniture
items.desc: Furniture made to your exact measurements, timber and finish. We survey the space, draw the piece, confirm it with you and only then start cutting.
items.meta: Built to your room, not to a catalogue
items.body: Every home has a corner no ready-made piece fits. We measure the space on site, draw the piece around it and build it in our own workshop, so the finished furniture uses the full width, the full height and the awkward angle as well. You choose the board, the laminate or veneer, the hardware and the finish. Nothing is ordered in and resold — it is manufactured here in Nagpur, which is why changes mid-way are possible and why the fit is exact.

items.title: Modular Kitchen
items.desc: Complete modular kitchens — layout planning, carcass, shutters, hardware, counter coordination and on-site installation.
items.body: A modular kitchen is judged after five years, not on the day it is installed. We plan the work triangle around how your family actually cooks, use moisture-resistant board where water reaches, and fit hinges and channels that carry a written warranty. Shutter options run from budget laminate through acrylic and high-gloss to matte PU. Tall units, corner solutions, pull-out baskets, chimney and hob coordination and lighting are all planned before manufacturing begins.

items.title: Modular Wardrobes
items.desc: Hinged and sliding wardrobes with internal organisers, drawers, mirror units and loft storage, built to the wall.
items.body: A built-to-wall wardrobe recovers the dead space a loose almirah wastes — above it, behind it and beside it. We plan the internals around what you own: hanging heights for sarees and for shirts, drawer banks for folded clothes, a locker section, and loft storage for luggage and bedding. Hinged shutters for a tight room, sliding shutters where a swinging door would block the walkway.

items.title: Home Furniture
items.desc: Complete home furnishing under one roof, matched in timber and finish across every room so the house reads as one piece of work.
items.meta: Sofas, beds, dining, TV units and storage
items.body: Buying room by room from different shops is what leaves a house looking assembled rather than designed. We supply the whole home — living, bedrooms, dining, kitchen and storage — matched in timber tone, finish and hardware. It also means one point of contact, one delivery schedule and one team installing.

items.title: Office Furniture
items.desc: Office interiors and furniture for new offices, clinics, showrooms and commercial spaces, planned around headcount and layout.
items.body: Office furniture has to survive eight hours a day of use and still look presentable to a visitor. We build linear and cluster workstations, manager tables, conference tables, reception counters, storage and file units, and supply seating to match. Cable routing, partition heights and circulation are planned before manufacture.

items.title: TV Units
items.desc: Wall-mounted and floor-standing TV units with concealed storage, back panelling, profile lighting and cable management.
items.body: A TV unit is the first thing a guest looks at in a living room. We build the full wall as one composition — panelling, open display shelving, closed storage below, profile lighting behind — and route every cable inside so nothing hangs down the wall. Finishes range from veneer and laminate through to resin and high-gloss.

items.title: Sofa Sets & L-Corner Sofas
items.desc: Sofa sets in 3+2, 3+1+1 and L-corner layouts, in fabric or leatherette, with a seat firmness you actually pick.
items.meta: Frames, foam and fabric to your choice
items.body: A sofa is a frame, a foam and a fabric, and shops usually only let you choose the fabric. We build the frame in seasoned timber to the length your room takes, set the seat depth and firmness to your preference, and let you choose fabric or leatherette from the sample books. L-corner layouts can be built handed either way, so the chaise sits on the side that suits the room.

items.title: Beds & Hydraulic Beds
items.desc: King, queen and single beds — plain, box-storage or hydraulic-lift — with matching side tables and headboard panelling.
items.meta: Storage where a bedroom needs it most
items.body: The area under a bed is the largest unused storage volume in most Indian homes. A hydraulic bed lifts the whole mattress platform on gas pistons so the entire space is reachable in one motion, which is what makes it usable for bedding and luggage. We build plain, box-storage and hydraulic versions with upholstered or panelled headboards to match the wardrobe.

items.title: Dining Tables & Dining Sets
items.desc: Dining tables and complete sets in solid timber, veneer or glass-top, sized so chairs still pull out comfortably.
items.meta: 4, 6 and 8 seaters to suit the room
items.body: Most dining sets are bought too large for the room and the chairs end up against the wall. We size the table to the clearance actually available, then build it — 4, 6 or 8 seater, round or rectangular, solid timber, veneer or glass-top. Chairs can be cushioned or plain and are finished to match.

items.title: CNC Mandir / Pooja Mandir
items.desc: Home temples in Sagwan and other timbers, with CNC-cut jaali panels, storage drawers and integrated lighting.
items.meta: CNC-cut jaali work and Sagwan mandirs
items.body: A mandir is the one piece in the house that is looked at every single day, so the detail matters more than the size. We cut jaali and pillar detailing on CNC for a clean, repeatable pattern, then hand-finish it. Wall-mounted and floor-standing units, with drawers for pooja items, a shelf for the samai and concealed lighting. Sagwan (teak) is the usual choice for its grain and its life.

items.title: Custom Storage Solutions
items.desc: Storage built into the space you have — crockery units, shoe racks, loft storage, utility and study units.
items.meta: Crockery, shoe, loft and utility units
items.body: Storage is what a house runs out of first. We build into the spaces already there: under the stairs, above the door, the passage wall, the utility balcony. Crockery units, shoe racks, loft boxes, study tables with overhead storage and pantry units, all finished to match the surrounding work.

items.title: Interior Furniture Work
items.desc: Complete interior furniture work for homes and offices — panelling, partitions, false ceiling coordination and built-ins.
items.meta: Full interior fit-outs, not just pieces
items.body: When a whole flat or office is being done, the furniture, the panelling and the services have to be sequenced together. We take on complete interior furniture work: wall panelling, partitions, built-in storage, wardrobe and kitchen, coordinated with your electrical and false ceiling contractors so nothing is cut open afterwards.

items.title: Furniture Manufacturing
items.desc: We manufacture rather than resell — which is why customisation is possible and why the quality is ours to answer for.
items.meta: Made in our own Nagpur workshop
items.body: We are a manufacturing unit, not a reselling showroom. Boards are cut, edge-banded, assembled and finished in our own workshop at Godhani Road. That is what makes a non-standard size, a changed shutter or a different internal layout possible at all, and it is why we can stand behind the workmanship instead of forwarding a complaint to a supplier. Bulk and repeat orders for builders and offices are welcome.

items.title: Custom Furniture Design
items.desc: Design consultation with layout drawings, material samples and finish options, so you approve the piece before it is built.
items.meta: Drawings and samples before you commit
items.body: You should not have to imagine what you are paying for. We prepare layout drawings and elevations for the piece, put the actual laminate, veneer and hardware samples in front of you, and confirm the finish in writing before the board is cut. Changes at the drawing stage cost nothing; changes after manufacture cost a great deal.

items.title: Delivery & Installation
items.desc: Delivery and on-site installation across Nagpur by our own fitters, with the site cleaned up before they leave.
items.meta: Delivered and fitted by our own team
items.body: Furniture is easy to damage between the workshop and the wall. Our own team handles delivery and installation — levelling, wall fixing, shutter and hinge adjustment, hardware fitting and a final clean-up. Availability and charges depend on the site and the location; both are confirmed in writing with your quotation.

props.sub: Practical advice on choosing kitchens, wardrobes, sofas, beds and dining sets — written from what we are actually asked in the showroom.

props.heading: Furniture guides & buying advice
props.sub: Nine guides covering the decisions that matter before you order.

posts.title: How to Choose the Right Modular Kitchen for Your Home
posts.excerpt: Layout, carcass material, shutter finish and hardware — what actually decides whether a modular kitchen lasts.
posts.body:
Start with the layout, not the finish. An L-shape suits most Indian kitchens; a U-shape works where three walls are free; a parallel layout suits a narrow room; an island needs at least a metre of clearance on every side, which most flats do not have.

Then the carcass. This is the part nobody sees and the part that fails first. Anywhere water reaches — under the sink, beside the hob — use moisture-resistant ply or HDHMR rather than ordinary MDF. Ask what the carcass is, not just what the shutter is.

Shutters are the visible choice: laminate is the most economical and the most durable against daily wear; acrylic and high-gloss give a reflective, seamless face; matte PU hides fingerprints best. Consider who cleans the kitchen and how often before choosing a high-gloss dark shade.

Hardware decides the daily experience. Soft-close hinges and channels from a brand that gives a written warranty are worth the difference, because a failed channel on a loaded drawer is a repair, not an inconvenience.

Finally, plan the services before manufacture: chimney duct route, hob gas point, water inlet and outlet, and at least two spare power points on the counter.

posts.title: Modular Wardrobe vs Traditional Wardrobe — Which Is Better?
posts.excerpt: A loose almirah can be moved; a modular wardrobe uses every inch. Which one is right depends on whether you own the house.
posts.body:
A traditional loose almirah is a piece of furniture; a modular wardrobe is part of the room. That single difference drives everything else.

Space is the clearest argument for modular. A loose almirah wastes the gap above it, the gap behind it and the gap beside it — often a third of the wall. A built-to-wall wardrobe takes the full floor-to-ceiling height, with loft storage above for luggage and bedding.

Internals are the second. A modular wardrobe is planned around what you actually own: long hanging for sarees and coats, short hanging for shirts, drawer banks for folded clothes, a locker section for valuables. An almirah gives you one rod and one shelf.

The case for traditional: it moves with you. If you are in a rented flat or expect to shift within a few years, a loose almirah is the sensible choice, and it needs no installation.

Cost is closer than people expect. A modular wardrobe costs more up front but is priced per square foot of the wall it covers, and it replaces the almirah, the loft boxes and the dressing unit at once.

If you own the home, build it in. If you may move, buy loose.

posts.title: How to Choose the Perfect Sofa Size for Your Living Room
posts.excerpt: Measure the walkway before the wall. The commonest mistake is a sofa that fits the wall but blocks the room.
posts.body:
Measure the walkway first. You need about 75–90 cm of clear passage in front of the sofa, and about 40–45 cm between the sofa and the centre table. Fit those first, and whatever length is left over is your sofa — not the other way round.

As a rough guide, a three-seater runs about 6 to 7 feet, a two-seater about 4 to 5 feet, and a single about 3 feet. An L-corner will seat more people in the same floor area than a 3+2, because it uses the corner a straight sofa leaves empty.

Check the door before you order. A sofa that fits the living room but not the staircase turn is a common and expensive discovery. Built-to-order frames can be made in sections and assembled inside — say so at the drawing stage.

Seat depth matters more than length for comfort. A deeper seat suits lounging; a shallower one suits sitting upright and is easier for elders to rise from. Decide which the room is for.

Finally, sit on the foam before confirming. Firmness is a choice, and it is the one thing you cannot change later without re-upholstering.

posts.title: Things to Consider Before Buying a New Bed
posts.excerpt: Storage type, mattress size, headboard and piston rating — the four decisions that matter, in order.
posts.body:
Decide the storage type first, because it changes the whole build. A plain bed is the cheapest and lightest. A box bed gives storage through small side or top flaps, usable for things you rarely need. A hydraulic bed lifts the entire mattress platform on gas pistons, opening the whole area in one motion — this is the only version where the space is genuinely usable week to week.

Fix the mattress size before the frame. 6x6.5 ft for a king, 5x6.5 ft for a queen, 3x6.5 ft for a single. Build the frame to the mattress, not the other way round, or you will be hunting for a non-standard mattress for years.

Check the piston rating on a hydraulic bed. The pistons must be rated for the weight of your mattress; an under-rated piston will not hold the platform up, which is both a nuisance and a hazard. Ask for the rating in writing.

Measure the room, not just the bed. You want walking space on at least one long side, and enough clearance for the wardrobe shutters to open fully.

Lastly, plan the headboard with the wall. A headboard, back panelling and side tables built as one composition costs little more than the bed alone and finishes the room.

posts.title: How to Choose the Right Dining Table for Your Family
posts.excerpt: Size it to the clearance, not to the seat count you wish you had.
posts.body:
Size the table to the clearance, not to the number of guests you occasionally host. You need about 90 cm between the table edge and the nearest wall so a chair can be pulled out and someone can walk behind it. Measure that first.

Per seat, allow about 60 cm of table edge. A six-seater therefore runs roughly 6ft x 3ft; a four-seater about 3ft x 3ft or 4ft x 2.5ft. Round tables seat people more sociably and have no sharp corners, which matters with small children; rectangular tables fit narrow rooms better.

Choose the top for how the family eats. Solid timber is the most durable and can be re-polished after years of use. Veneer gives the same look for less, but cannot be sanded back as often. Toughened glass is the easiest to clean and suits a modern room, but shows every fingerprint.

Chairs decide comfort. Cushioned seats suit long meals; plain timber is easier to clean with children. Check that the chair slides under the table when pushed in — if it does not, the room will feel crowded.

If the dining area is tight, a wall-side or corner layout recovers a surprising amount of floor.

posts.title: Customised Furniture vs Ready-Made Furniture — Which Should You Choose?
posts.excerpt: Ready-made wins on time and price. Customised wins on fit, material honesty and anything non-standard.
posts.body:
Ready-made furniture wins on two things: it is available today, and it is cheaper, because it is made in volume to one size. If your room is a standard shape and you need it this week, buy ready-made.

Customised wins everywhere else. It fits the space exactly, including the awkward corner, the low beam and the wall that is not quite square. You choose the carcass material rather than accepting whatever is inside — which matters most in kitchens and wardrobes, where the hidden board decides the life of the piece. And you can have internals planned around what you actually own.

The usual objection is time. A customised piece takes longer, because it is drawn, approved and then manufactured. Plan for that in your schedule rather than being surprised by it.

The usual misconception is cost. Customised is not automatically more expensive: you are not paying for a showroom markup, and one built-in wardrobe often replaces an almirah, loft boxes and a dressing unit.

A practical middle path: customise the built-ins — kitchen, wardrobes, TV unit, mandir — and buy loose pieces like chairs ready-made.

posts.title: Best Furniture for Modern Homes in Nagpur
posts.excerpt: What actually suits Nagpur flats: the climate, the room sizes and the storage problem.
posts.body:
Nagpur homes have three constants worth designing around: a long, hot, dry summer, a concentrated monsoon, and flats where storage runs out before floor space does.

The climate argues for moisture-resistant board in kitchens, utility areas and any wardrobe on an external wall, and for finishes that tolerate heat without lifting — good-quality laminate and PU rather than the cheapest available. Solid timber pieces should be properly seasoned before use, or joints open up when the dry season arrives.

Room sizes argue for built-ins. Floor-to-ceiling wardrobes, a TV unit built as a wall composition, a hydraulic bed and storage built under the stairs and along passages will recover more usable space than any amount of rearranging loose furniture.

For the living room, an L-corner sofa built to the actual corner seats more people in the same area than a 3+2. For the kitchen, an L-shape suits most flats here.

And for the one piece almost every home here wants — a mandir — plan its wall early, with a power point for lighting, rather than fitting it in at the end.

posts.title: How to Plan Custom Furniture for a New Home
posts.excerpt: Sequence matters. Plan the furniture before the electrical, not after.
posts.body:
Plan the furniture before the electrical work, not after. Where the TV unit, bed, wardrobe, kitchen appliances and mandir sit decides where power, data and light points must go. Deciding afterwards means chasing walls that have just been finished.

Start with a measured plan of every room, including window heights, beam positions, door swings and the existing electrical points. Mark the fixed things you cannot move.

Then work room by room in priority order: kitchen and wardrobes first, since they take the longest and affect the services most; then beds and the TV wall; then dining and loose furniture; then the mandir wall, which needs its own light point.

Choose materials once, across the whole house. A single laminate and hardware family used everywhere costs less than choosing per room and makes the home read as one piece of work.

Approve drawings and physical samples before manufacture. A change on a drawing is free; a change after cutting is not.

Finally, sequence delivery against your civil work. Furniture delivered before the flooring and painting are finished will be damaged.

posts.title: Things to Check Before Buying Modular Furniture
posts.excerpt: Nine questions that separate furniture that lasts from furniture that looks good on delivery day.
posts.body:
Ask what the carcass is made of. This is the board you never see and the part that fails first. Moisture-resistant ply or HDHMR in wet areas; ordinary MDF is not acceptable under a sink.

Ask about edge banding. Unbanded or thinly banded edges swell the moment they meet water. 2mm banding on exposed edges is worth asking for by name.

Ask which hardware brand, and what warranty is written on the quotation. Hinges and channels are what you operate every day.

Ask whether it is manufactured or bought in. A unit that makes its own furniture can change a size or a layout mid-way and has to answer for the quality itself.

Ask to see the finish sample in daylight, not under showroom lighting.

Ask what the quotation excludes — counter material, electrical, chimney, transport and installation are the usual omissions that appear later.

Ask how the site is measured, and whether you approve a drawing before cutting.

Ask about the delivery and installation timeline in writing.

And ask what happens after installation: who comes back to adjust a shutter that has settled, and for how long.
